samples.summary: Label removal fires on fail-safe resolutions, clearing a truthful `ci-config-changed` label when the resolver did not actually determine what changed
samples.evidence: The new `else if (areas)` branch (ci-report.yml:280) removes the label whenever `areas` parsed and `areas.ciConfig` is falsy. Its comment claims "Only when `areas` parsed. A missing resolution means we do not know what changed" — but a *parsed* resolution is not the same as a *determined* one. `scripts/changed-areas.mjs`'s `FULL()` helper (line 470-477) returns `{ full: true, ..., ciConfig: false }` for every fail-safe route: "no diff base could be resolved" (line 546), "could not diff <base>...<head>" (line 550), "could not read the CI mapping" (line 542) and "WAFFLEBASE_CHANGED_AREAS was not a resolution object" (line 525). That object is exactly what `ci.yml` writes into `ci-context/areas.json`. So on a run where the diff failed, a PR that genuinely edits `harness.config.json`/`.github/workflows/**` gets its label REMOVED, i.e. the label is cleared in precisely the "we don't know" state the comment says is excluded. The condition should also require that the run reached `classify()` (e.g. `areas.full === false || areas.ciConfig === true`, or an explicit `determined` flag), not merely that `areas` is non-null.

samples.summary: Label removal can now mutate the wrong pull request when `prNumber` came from the commit-association fallback
samples.evidence: `prNumber` may be resolved by `listPullRequestsAssociatedWithCommit` and then `data.find((p) => p.state === 'open')?.number ?? data[0]?.number` (ci-report.yml:150), which can pick a closed/merged or otherwise unrelated PR for that head sha. Previously the only label write was additive (`addLabels`); the new `removeLabel` branch (line 284) makes a wrong `prNumber` destructive — it strips `ci-config-changed` from a PR this run says nothing about. Low impact (advisory label) but it is a new state-mutating path guarded only by a best-effort PR lookup.

samples.summary: `pull_request_target` can never resolve refs: the head sha is not present in a base-ref checkout, so that branch always degrades to a full run
samples.evidence: `resolveRefs` handles `pull_request_target` in the same branch as `pull_request` (line 280) and hard-requires `verified(payload.pull_request?.head?.sha)` (lines 284-285), returning `null` when the sha is absent from the checkout. For `pull_request_target`, `actions/checkout` checks out the BASE ref by default and does not fetch the fork's head commit, so `verified(head)` is null on essentially every such run and the function returns `null` → `resolve()` reports "no diff base could be resolved" → full suite. The direction is safe, but the branch is now dead code that silently disables the filter for that event; if any workflow ever adopts `pull_request_target`, it will look supported and never filter. Falling back to a fetched `refs/pull/N/head` or documenting the limitation would be clearer.

samples.summary: `push` head silently falls back to the checked-out `HEAD` when `payload.after` cannot be verified, mixing a payload-derived base with a checkout-derived head
samples.evidence: `const head = verified(payload.after) ?? "HEAD";` (line 305). The whole point of the change is that the head must come from the payload and never from the checkout (see the file's own note at lines 167-172 and the test at scripts/test/changed-areas.test.mjs asserting "a missing head must fail safe, not silently become the checkout" for pull_request). The `push` path keeps exactly the fallback the pull_request path was fixed to remove: if `after` is missing or not present in the checkout (deleted branch push where `after` is all-zeroes, or a checkout at a different ref), the diff is taken against whatever HEAD happens to be rather than failing safe to `null`. Also note the all-zeroes guard at line 303 is applied only to `before`, not to `after`.
